items.quote: Our implementation of grant types and access tokens follows OAuth 2.0 specifications.
items.why: Says OAuth 2.0 implemented; nothing on bearer_token.

items.quote: This grant type is designed for situations when the client (your app) is acting on its own behalf, not a user.
items.why: Describes app-only grant only; no oauth2 overall or bearer_token.

items.quote: Once your app is approved for Trial access you can generate a token to test the API without setting up the Oauth flow.
items.why: Test token without OAuth flow; supports bearer side only, not full claim.

items.quote: Application requests are reviewed by Pinterest.
items.why: Says Pinterest reviews app requests, which is the approval gate.

items.quote: If approved for API use, your app receives Trial access, which is best for exploring our API features.
items.why: Approval yields Trial access; implies gate but does not state it.

items.quote: Your app must already be approved for Trial access and comply with our Developer Guidelines.
items.why: Prerequisite for Standard access; not a statement of the approval gate.

items.quote: Prepare a video recording of your app completing an action using the Pinterest API.
items.why: Demo video is part of Standard review; related to approval, not the gate itself.

items.quote: Pinterest API services are only available to authenticated and authorized users.
items.why: Authentication requirement only; says nothing about REST or API breadth.

items.quote: Pinterest is bringing its data and Ads capabilities directly into the AI tools teams already use.
items.why: Suggests official AI-tool integration; never names an MCP server or the URL.
